chunks: From him, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Muskhan, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a garden in which a slave or a hired worker is present, who owns nothing of the garden, and a man takes from his garden. He said: 'If he is in this position, owning nothing of the garden, then I dislike that I take anything from him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on taking produce from a garden worker who has no ownership stake?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the specific case of a slave or hired laborer who possesses no ownership stake in the garden they cultivate. He advises that if the worker holds no proprietary right to the produce, the owner should refrain from taking from the worker's share, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ihsan* (benevolence) and fair distribution beyond strict contractual obligation. This ruling highlights the ethical dimension of labor rights in Islamic jurisprudence, where the employer's generosity is encouraged to ensure the worker's well-being.
